scope_contract.goal_statement: To monitor facility and device status.

claims.content: The Operator accesses the facility and device status display.
The Operator accesses the facility and device status display.
The system presents a GUI display of the I-15 Reversible Lane Control System facility geographic area, including the layout of the mainline I-15 and SR-163 freeway area.

The system displays facility status information, including facility status (e.g., Open or Closed), current direction of traffic flow, customer eligibility, and current facility boundaries extending one mile in either direction.
The system displays device sensor status using dynamic icons for all field device sensors and controllers.
The system receives current device status information from field devices within 2 seconds of the status being issued.
The system checks each received status against alarm conditions for that device sensor and updates the status to indicate an alarm when an alarm condition exists.
The system refreshes the status display every 2 seconds.
The Operator views the current facility and device status information, including displayed alarm conditions and override states, on the GUI.

The GUI provides the ability to display the status of one device at the detail level, showing all sensor data for that device, and to display the current status of a category of devices at the detail level, showing all sensor data for all devices of the same category.

When a device status has been overridden to continue an operating sequence after an intermediate device control failure, the system displays that overridden device status on the screen with a color different from the normal and alarm status colors, and the operating sequence continues to the end.

Exception 1 — Divergence at main flow step 6 (alarm condition check): If an alarm status occurs for a device, the RLCS detects the alarm condition within 2 seconds; the GUI issues an audible alarm, displays an icon different from the okay status, and changes the color of the affected device.

Exception 2 — Divergence at main flow step 6 (active alarm): The GUI allows the operator to acknowledge an alarm and to silence the audible portion of the alarm for a configurable number of seconds or permanently for that device only.
Exception 3 — Divergence at main flow step 6 (alarm condition): In the event of an alarm condition, the system displays appropriate emergency contact information.
Exception 4 — Divergence at main flow step 6 (alarm condition cleared): When the alarm condition is removed, the alarm icon automatically changes back to the normal status icon.
Exception 5 — Divergence at main flow step 5 (device status receipt): Failure to receive a valid status after a configurable number of retries is considered a device failure.

documented continuation or exit after an alarm condition clears and the icon returns to normal
documented recovery or continuation after a device is classified as failed due to exhausted status retries
documented retry mechanism for missing or invalid device statuses before the configured retry limit
Evidence supporting that the use case returns to main flow step 7 to continue monitored display refresh.
Documented recovery or continuation after a device is classified as failed due to exhausted status retries.
Evidence supporting that the use case returns to main flow step 7 to continue refresh and monitoring.

claims.content: The GUI displays the facility geographic area layout and current facility and device status information to the Operator, including facility status, traffic flow direction, customer eligibility, boundaries, device sensor status, alarm conditions, and override states.
The GUI provides the ability to display the status of one device at the detail level, showing all sensor data for that device.
The current status of the selected category of devices is displayed at the detail level, showing all sensor data for all devices of the same category (e.g., gates, pop-ups, CMS devices).

quality_flags.detail: [exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception Flow claims 0-3 describe alarm detection/indication, alarm acknowledgement/silencing, emergency-contact display, and alarm clearing, but none states whether the flow returns to a main-flow step (e.g., refresh/monitoring), hands off, terminates, or ends in an explicit terminal state. Only claim 4 ('considered a device failure') documents a clear failure outcome. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that the monitoring flow continues after alarm detection/indication or after operator acknowledgement/silencing, emergency-contact display, or alarm clearing; and that facility map and status information continue to display/refresh specifically after those branches.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 1 (alarm condition check) describes detecting the alarm and displaying audible/visual indications, but it does not state whether the flow returns to a main_flow step, terminates/hands off, or reaches an explicit terminal state. Alarm indication alone is not a clear exit outcome. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Evidence that after alarm indicators are displayed the exception flow returns to main flow step 7 or otherwise explicitly resumes/continues the main flow.; Evidence that monitoring specifically continues every 2 seconds after the alarm response.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 2 (active alarm acknowledgement/silencing) describes that the operator can acknowledge and silence the alarm, but it does not document what happens afterward—return to main_flow, terminate, or hand off. This leaves the branch without a clear outcome. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that status information continues to display and is continually updated after acknowledgement or silencing.; Explicit evidence for the exception flow's recovery or exit behavior after acknowledgement or silencing.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 3 (emergency contact display) only says the system displays contact information; it does not state whether the flow returns to a main_flow step, terminates/hands off, or reaches a terminal state. (still no supporting evidence after retrieval)

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 4 (alarm cleared) says the alarm icon returns to normal, but it does not explicitly state that the flow returns to main_flow step 7/8 or otherwise terminates. The branch lacks a documented continuation/exit after clearing. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that the use case resumes the main flow or resumes continuous facility and device status monitoring after the alarm condition is cleared.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 1 describes alarm detection and audible/visual indication after main flow step 6, but it does not state whether the flow returns to a main_flow step, terminates, or ends in another explicit outcome.
[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 2 allows the operator to acknowledge and silence an alarm, but it does not specify what happens afterward (return to main flow, terminate, or hand off).
[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 3 displays emergency contact information on an alarm condition but does not specify a return to main flow, termination, handoff, or terminal state.
[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception 4 says the alarm icon returns to normal when the alarm clears, but it does not explicitly return to a main_flow step or state a terminal/handoff outcome.

inconsistency_hints: The goal claim includes 'process requests for changing field device status,' which is outside the use case name and explicitly excluded in the goal scope contract. The main flow only monitors/displays status and never processes change requests, so the goal is over-broad and conflates a separate use case.

Alternative Flow claim 0 describes an overridden-device display condition but does not identify any main_flow step as the divergence point. The coverage note suggests step 4, but the claim itself and its cited evidence do not establish an attachment point.

Postconditions 2 and 3 require detail-level display of a selected individual device or selected device category, but the Main Flow only covers the overview display and never includes selecting a device/category or displaying detail-level sensor data. These postconditions are therefore not reachable from the main flow as written.

The Main Flow only presents and refreshes the overview status; it has no step where the Operator selects a single device or a device category to produce the detail-level displays. Thus Postconditions 1 and 2 (single-device detail and category detail with all sensor data) are not reachable from the described flow.
